For instance, if a bank holds $1 million in cash today, by the end of the year, that amount might only maintain its purchasing power if the inflation rate is zero, which has not been the case historically. 

Moreover, banks need to keep a portion of their assets in liquid form to meet customer withdrawals and other immediate financial obligations, reducing the amount available for investment or additional risk-taking.
